core_obligations: Set I to the ideal generated by f_1 to f_n and let a relation among the images of g_1 to g_m in A/I be given (proof lines 7627-7629).
Because I is generated by the f_i, lift that relation to a relation in A involving all n+m elements (proof lines 7629-7634).
Apply the hypothesis that the long sequence is H_1-regular to decompose the lifted relation into trivial relations in A (proof lines 7634-7635).
Take images in A/I to obtain a decomposition of the original relation into trivial relations, which is H_1-regularity of the images of g_1 to g_m (proof lines 7635-7637).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is the truncation statement for H_1-regularity: the images of the last m elements of an H_1-regular sequence in the quotient by the ideal generated by the first n elements form an H_1-regular sequence (statement lines 7618-7623). The proof is a 12-line argument (proof lines 7626-7637) whose strategy is to reduce H_1-regularity to the existence of a decomposition of every relation into trivial relations: a relation among the images in A/I is lifted to a relation among all n+m elements in A by using that I is generated by f_1 to f_n, and then the hypothesis that the long sequence is H_1-regular provides a decomposition of that lifted relation into trivial relations, whose image in A/I gives the required decomposition of the original relation. The point that has to be seen is that the lift exists at all, which is the content of choosing coefficients b_i for the f_i; the rest of the proof is taking images.
